activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Limits of Radical Functions Using Conjugate Multiplication

feedback.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 81}\frac{\sqrt{x}-9}{x-81} & =\frac{\sqrt{81}-9}{81-81}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 81}\frac{\sqrt{x}-9}{x-81} & ={lim}_{x\to 81}\frac{(\sqrt{x}-9)(\sqrt{x}+9)}{(x-81)(\sqrt{x}+9)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 81}\frac{{(\sqrt{x})}^{2}-{9}^{2}}{(x-81)(\sqrt{x}+9)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 81}\frac{x-81}{(x-81)(\sqrt{x}+9)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 81}\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}+9} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{81}+9} \\  & =\frac{1}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$
